proven: Real backend fault becomes a store string, not a fake throw-only checkpoint.
Natural failure storage error remains visible rather than being overwritten by a recovery-success explanation.
Actual pause stops and reports checkpoint storage error without rejecting its pause promise.
Same Goal ID/task ID/round retained; paused/interrupted state and runner exit remain honest; no automatic verifier, new round/task/resume occurs.

After natural failed direct write error, the previously valid persisted terminal checkpoint is loaded from backend and hydrated; explicit recovery runs only summary, logical calls3→4, one file read and one file write.
Owned output file inode/mtime/hash unchanged across explicit recovery; used model calls remain accounted.
Adjacent existing store and UI task-completion-write-failure regressions remain green.
notProven: Freshness of every stale checkpoint or blocking every possible resume after an earlier durable snapshot exists.
Elimination of all replay risks under storage corruption, concurrent writers or process death.
Native desktop AX/installation/signing, actual SQLite disk faults, external model/provider availability or full same-Goal native recovery.
limits: Synthetic backend is real production store contract with injected backend rejection; it is not the native SQLite driver.
Natural-failure fault injection is deliberately restricted to paused/interrupted checkpoint writes because task finally already persists the terminal snapshot while still running.
Pause fault may also reject task finally writes after interruption; both are stopped/error states and no user resume is attempted in that test.
No schemas, ledger rules, permission rules, state machine gates, task identity or recovery-freshness gate are changed.
The patch remains only under /tmp and has not been applied to repository or pushed.
